title: Chibi office woman with Meshy, from your two pictures
question: How close is dressed-nopose to your picture, and should we keep going with Meshy for this style?

media.caption: Your brief: "Try making this model, both manually and with meshy" (this is the Meshy side; another agent is building it by hand in Blender). Every attempt in the order made, beside its reference picture: front, her left 3/4, her left side, back. Same Blender camera and soft light for all.

Faces close up, front and her left 3/4. On all five the eyes are crisp, flat and painted on the head surface; none tilts forward on its own edge like the Meshy Mio did. On the square base head, her right eye (image left) wraps round the head's corner when turned.
dressed-nopose rigged (Meshy auto-rig), in the live viewer with the game idle and walk. The walk is Mio's clip, so the steps are high for these short legs and the head leans forward in the side view.
What Meshy got: your pictures with the background and floor shadow cut away (BiRefNet on the CPU). Nothing else changed.
The base body picture, cut the same way.

options.label: 1. dressed
options.note: Meshy image-to-3D, latest model, textured in the same task, no remesh, image enhancement off, no PBR, 4k texture, pose_mode a-pose (the settings of the earlier Mio meshy-single, plus a-pose). 30 credits, 815,874 triangles. Shape, hair, collar, skirt and shoes match; the a-pose spread the arms and turned the mitten hands into flat hands with thumbs. Too many faces for Meshy's auto-rig (limit 320,000), so not rigged. Extra images: Meshy's own previews.

options.label: 2. base
options.note: The base body picture, same settings as 1. 30 credits, 173,026 triangles. Square head and stubby legs kept; the a-pose again gave flat hands with fingers instead of round mittens.

options.label: 3. dressed-t2
options.note: Same picture as 1, Smart Topology instead (meshy-t2, target 3,000 faces, textured, 4k, a-pose). 15 credits, 3,204 triangles, game-light. Hands stayed closer to mittens. The hair is faceted with jagged tips at the back, a small mark on the back of the head and a dark seam on the blouse back. Rigged (Meshy auto-rig, height 1.0 m, 5 credits): in the live viewer.

options.label: 4. base-nopose
options.note: 2 with one change: no pose_mode (the arms stay as in your picture). 30 credits, 182,858 triangles. Round mitten hands kept. Rigged (5 credits): in the live viewer.

options.label: 5. dressed-nopose
options.note: 1 with one change: no pose_mode. 30 credits, 689,416 triangles. The closest to your picture: mitten hands, arms slightly out, collar, skirt, flats, bob with the side-swept fringe. Differences: the blouse renders whiter and the skirt blacker than your grey; hair a little darker. Rigged from a copy decimated to 60,000 faces in Blender (UVs and texture kept), Meshy auto-rig on that file, 5 credits; the decimation shows as slightly rough hair tips at the back in the viewer.

links.label: Turn dressed-nopose, dressed-t2 and base-nopose, play the game idle and walk, one beside the other (live 3D)
Credits spent: Meshy 150 (five generations 135, three rigs 15; the full dressed rig was refused at no cost), balance 1,285
